chunks: Al-Shaykh Abu 'Abd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Everything that falls into the well which has no blood, such as scorpions, beetles, and the like, then there is no harm.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well into which the creature falls
key_terms.الْخَنَافِسِ: beetles, another example of creatures without flowing blood
key_terms.الْعَقَارِبِ: scorpions, given as an example of such creatures
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood; here meaning flowing blood whose absence affects the ruling
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating legal permissibility or no impurity concern

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a creature without flowing blood falls into a well and dies in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning things without flowing blood that fall into a well and die in it. It states that creatures such as scorpions and beetles do not cause a problem in the well water, indicating no impurity or objection in this case.
